item.title: Buena Vista Social Club — Sat Sep 26, 2:00 PM — DPAC Presented by First Horizon
item.description:
A Remarkable Blend of Music, Dance and Heart It’s been years since legendary singer Omara Portuondo last entered a recording studio. Once known as the “Queen of Feeling,” her voice was celebrated throughout Cuba – until she vanished from the spotlight. But when an ambitious young record producer brings her a rare opportunity, the elusive diva must finally reckon with her past. Hailed as a “jaw-dropping, soul-stirring must see” (The Washington Post), the Tony® and GRAMMY® Award-winning BUENA VISTA SOCIAL CLUB™ is a journey through music and memory into the beating heart of Havana. A world-class company brings the story of the iconic album to thrilling life in this tale of big dreams, second chances, and music that needs no translation.

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Sep 26, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.

item.title: CEE Seminar - Explaining the Exposome: Accumulation of Novel and Known PFASs in Living Things — Mon Sep 28, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: The pace of production for new and existing synthetic chemicals is continually increasing, rapidly outpacing our capacity to assess risks of exposure to these substances. Studies of the chemical exposome (chemicals accumulated in the body over a lifetime of exposure) have reported the presence of thousands of synthetic substances in human blood and these exposures likely contribute a significant portion of chronic disease risk in the general population; however, we lack critical information on where these chemicals come from, how they accumulate in the body, and implications for human health. Here I will discuss my research group's work towards answering the question: How does molecular structure impact a chemical's potential to accumulate in the body, and how can we use this knowledge to prioritize chemicals of concern during nontarget analysis (NTA)? item.title: Participatory Deportation Defense: Becoming Abogades de Confianza — Mon Sep 28, 12:30 PM — Perkins Library 218
item.description:
Focusing on the role that deportation defense lawyers play in legitimizing the deportation regime, this talk addresses the responsibilities lawyers have when representing people within an unjust legal system. What does it mean for an immigration lawyer to genuinely earn the trust of undocumented communities and become an abogade de confianza? Borja explores how lawyers can work alongside families, community organizers, and participatory defense campaigns to challenge detention and deportation. So doing, they can help center the leadership of criminalized people by supporting mutual aid efforts, court watch projects, and freedom campaigns. Borja's public talk casts light on what effective immigration advocacy can look like and encourages us to rethink the conventional wisdom that good legal representation alone is enough to produce justice.

item.title: Designing AI-Enabled Workflows — Mon Sep 28, 1:00 PM — The TEC - Technology Engagement Center
item.description:
Most AI projects don't fail because the technology isn't ready, they fail because the workflow around it was never designed with AI's actual strengths and limitations in mind. This workshop teaches you how to think before you build: how modern AI works at a conceptual level, where it excels, where it predictably breaks, and how it differs from traditional software. You'll learn a practical decision framework for determining whether AI, traditional automation, or a simple process improvement is the right answer for your use case.

item.title: RISE to the Challenge: Statistical Considerations for Rare Disease Clinical Investigations — Tue Sep 29, 9:00 AM — None
item.description:
This public workshop, co-convened by Duke Margolis and the FDA Rare Disease Innovation Hub, will explore statistical considerations in the design, conduct, and analysis of clinical investigations for rare disease medical products. The small patient populations inherent to rare disease present unique challenges that increase the risk of obtaining inconclusive trial results. Addressing these challenges requires careful attention to statistical rigor while utilizing tailored approaches that are necessary to make medical product development feasible in this space. Reliable and timely evidence that relies on data from all available information is critically important to patients and families affected by rare diseases, making the optimization of clinical investigation design, conduct, and analysis a matter of both scientific and ethical urgency.
The workshop will focus on key statistical considerations for tailored approaches employed across the full arc of rare disease development programs

item.title: Postdoc Research Communication Series: The Art of Research Communication — Tue Sep 29, 11:00 AM — Virtual
item.description:
